description: Literature review or research summary in Chinese or English. Separate what a source reports from the synthesis, compare methods and evidence, and explain disagreement and gaps.

rules.instruction: Keep each source report in its own sentences and mark where your synthesis starts.
rules.rationale: A reader must be able to see which claim belongs to a source and which claim belongs to the reviewer.

rules.instruction: Compare the method of each study before you compare its result.
rules.rationale: A result from two different methods answers two different questions. A direct comparison would overstate agreement or conflict.

rules.instruction: State the evidence strength that each cited source carries.
rules.rationale: A single case study and a controlled trial support the same sentence with very different force.

rules.instruction: When sources disagree, give the reason for the disagreement and do not average it away.
rules.rationale: A disagreement that is smoothed over hides a real open question and invents a consensus.

rules.instruction: Name the gaps that the reviewed literature leaves open.
rules.rationale: A review that reports no gap implies that the question is closed, which the evidence rarely supports.

rules.instruction: Keep the edition, date, location, and wording of each citation exact.
rules.rationale: A citation edit can change what a source says even when the sentence looks unchanged.

rules.instruction: Cite only a source that you read, and register its exact excerpt.
rules.rationale: A remembered or paraphrased source is not evidence, and it cannot be checked later.

rules.instruction: Group sources by question or method, not by the order in which you read them.
rules.rationale: A reading-order narrative hides the comparison that a review exists to provide.
